name: aumos
description: Investment methodologies you install and run as AI fund managers, under your own approval. Each plugin is an Aumos ManagerPackage: it proposes decisions and never sends an order — a person approves every one.

plugins.name: ai-hedge-fund-value
plugins.description: A port of ai-hedge-fund's deep-value pod: Graham, Buffett and Munger read the same point-in-time fundamentals independently, and one reconciliation weighs their convictions. Graham's view counts double, as the source's own strategy file specifies.

metadata.name: AI Hedge Fund — Deep Value
metadata.methodology: Three value analysts judge the same filed figures without seeing each other's answers, and their convictions are weighed into one judgement. Reasons from fundamentals and price alone — it is given no news and no thesis, because the harness it was ported from reads neither.

plugins.name: atlas-trend-crypto
plugins.description: Time-series momentum on crypto spot, in dollars. One or two assets and cash, because a basket of coins is one position wearing ten names. Holds only while the trend is up, sizes the exposure by realised volatility, and goes to cash when it is not. One monthly review, or nothing.

metadata.name: Atlas Trend Crypto
metadata.methodology: Scores BTC — and optionally ETH — on an ensemble of 1, 3, 6 and 12-month dollar returns, holds it only while that ensemble is positive, and scales the exposure to a volatility target. Everything not held is cash, not a stablecoin. Deliberately carries no inverse-volatility weighting or correlation scaling: the crypto universe has an effective breadth near one, and machinery that implies otherwise would be describing diversification this market does not have.

plugins.name: atlas-trend-kr
plugins.description: Time-series momentum across a fixed basket of Korea-listed ETFs, in won. Holds only what is trending in its own price, sizes what it holds by realised volatility, and parks in CD-rate funds when nothing is. One monthly rebalance, or nothing.

metadata.name: Atlas Trend KR
metadata.methodology: Scores five roles of Korea-listed ETF on an ensemble of 1, 3, 6 and 12-month won-denominated returns, holds only the positive ones at inverse-volatility weights under a portfolio volatility target, and puts everything else in a CD-rate fund. Hedged and unhedged share classes compete for the same role and are never held together. Returns one REBALANCE carrying the whole basket, or WAIT.

plugins.name: atlas-trend-us
plugins.description: Time-series momentum across a fixed basket of US-listed global ETFs. Holds only what is trending in its own price, sizes what it holds by realised volatility, and goes to T-bills when nothing is. One monthly rebalance, or nothing.

metadata.name: Atlas Trend US
metadata.methodology: Scores each ETF in a fixed multi-asset basket on an ensemble of 1, 3, 6 and 12-month total returns, holds only the positive ones at inverse-volatility weights under a portfolio volatility target, and puts everything else in short Treasuries. Returns one REBALANCE carrying the whole basket, or WAIT.

plugins.name: basic-investor
plugins.description: FinRobot's Data-CoT → Concept-CoT → Thesis-CoT, extended with Portfolio Context and a Decision stage. The reference ManagerPackage.

metadata.name: Basic Investor
metadata.methodology: Reads what the Skill Gateway will serve at asOf, reasons in three stages, and returns one DecisionProposal.

plugins.name: catalyst-turnaround
plugins.description: Korea-listed companies with an identifiable event that would repair the business and its balance sheet, held for as long as the event's own window and no longer. Keeps a catalyst ledger — scheduled, in progress, realised, delayed, failed — and never records a rising share price as a catalyst that worked.

metadata.name: Catalyst Turnaround
metadata.methodology: Registers a catalyst as a record with a primary source, a publication time, a confirmed or estimated window, the indicator that will confirm it, and the conditions that count as success and failure — all written before the window opens. Sizes from the distance to the price invalidation rather than from a cap, enters in stages that cannot be added twice on a re-run, and adjudicates success, delay or failure when the window arrives. A policy expectation with no traced path to this issuer's earnings stays a research candidate; a low valuation multiple is never a qualifying condition.

plugins.name: earnings-drift-watcher
plugins.description: Judges one thing only: whether the market has finished reacting to a reported surprise. Compares the reported figure against what was expected, then against how far the price has already travelled, and mostly concludes that it is too late.

metadata.name: Earnings Drift Watcher
metadata.methodology: Post-announcement drift, as a single question. Reads the reported figure against expectation, measures how much of the resulting move has already happened, and returns WATCH far more often than it returns anything else — because the answer to 'has the market finished reacting' is usually 'ask again later'.

plugins.name: evidence-gated
plugins.description: One evidence-gated methodology run as three market flows: a Korean sleeve, a US sleeve, and the allocator that sets their budgets and proposes the cross-market rebalance. The flows are subagents of one manager; only the orchestrator submits.

metadata.name: Evidence-Gated Allocator
metadata.methodology: One evidence-gated methodology run as three market flows: a Korean sleeve, a US sleeve, and the allocator that sets their budgets and proposes the cross-market rebalance. The flows are subagents of one manager; only the orchestrator submits.

plugins.name: fundamental-mean-reversion
plugins.description: Korea-listed single names whose price has fallen further than the damage to the business justifies. Researches the fall's causes before the chart, takes the recovery only after pre-registered stabilisation evidence, and names a target range that says whether it is a price band, a moving average or a valuation.

metadata.name: Fundamental Mean Reversion
metadata.methodology: Finds Korea-listed companies whose share price has fallen further than the damage to the business justifies, and takes the recovery toward a normal range only after stabilisation is confirmed. The technical state sets the order of research and is never the buy case; the buy case is a filing-level separation of a one-off charge from operating deterioration. Entry requires pre-registered stabilisation evidence, sizing carries a gap-and-halt haircut because a stop price is not a fill, staged additions never fire on price or elapsed time alone, and every position has a deadline it cannot be quietly reclassified out of.

plugins.name: prudent-allocator
plugins.description: Top-down and risk-budget-first. Starts from the book rather than from the asset, sizes every judgement by what a bad outcome costs the portfolio, and acts only when the exposure is wrong.

metadata.name: Prudent Allocator
metadata.methodology: Reads the book and the mandate first and the event second. Judges an event by what it does to the portfolio's downside, not by what it says about the asset, and returns one DecisionProposal.

plugins.name: shareholder-rerating
plugins.description: Korea-listed single equities whose earnings and capital headroom support a shareholder return programme that is actually being executed, held for the discount that closing it should close. Separates re-rating from dividends in every number, and never counts a company's buyback as the investor's income.

metadata.name: Shareholder Rerating
metadata.methodology: Judges whether a Korea-listed company's profit and capital support a shareholder return programme it is actually executing, and whether executing it closes the discount the shares trade at. Financials are read on capital above their own policy CET1 target, non-financials on cash after required investment. Announced and executed programmes are different facts; a company's buyback is never added to the investor's cash dividend.

plugins.name: undervalued-now
plugins.description: One paragraph, no capabilities, and its own web and shell. A benchmark of the model rather than of a methodology — the prompt is the question, and the forward return is the answer.

metadata.name: Undervalued Now
metadata.methodology: Asked to find one undervalued listed equity and propose a position in it, by whatever means it likes.
